summary: Describes a way to discover information about a web host, as well as about individual resources the host controls, from a well-known location. The host publishes a small metadata document, and clients can look there to find out how to interact with the site. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Before visiting a shop, you might read a small sign at the door saying what services it offers. This describes a standard sign that websites can post for programs to read.

questions: how to discover web host metadata
what is the well-known host-meta location
subtitle: A well-known file, /.well-known/host-meta, where a web host publishes metadata about itself and the resources it controls.

tldr.problem: Web protocols often need host-wide policy or metadata, but a host has no URI of its own, so people overloaded the root resource with data that did not belong to it.
tldr.mechanism: A client fetches the XRD document at /.well-known/host-meta over HTTP or HTTPS. It holds host-wide properties and links, plus link templates and lrdd links for resource-specific information.
tldr.outcome: Protocols get one common place to discover host metadata. A JSON form (JRD) is also defined, and applications that need authenticity must use HTTPS.

today: RFC 6415 is a Proposed Standard from October 2011. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction and Example
sections.content:
Web protocols often need to discover host policy or metadata, where the host is the entity that controls all resources with a common URI host (RFC 3986). Because a host has no URI or representation, per-resource methods such as HTTP headers are not available. This often led to overloading the root HTTP resource with host metadata that is not about that resource.

The RFC defines a lightweight metadata document, host-meta, and registers the well-known URI suffix host-meta under RFC 5785. Because host-wide scope can be too coarse, it adds two resource-specific mechanisms: link templates, which turn a resource URI into a link, and LRDD documents (Link-based Resource Descriptor Documents, pronounced 'lard'), which carry information that templates cannot express.

The example document has a host-wide copyright link and a host property, plus hub, lrdd and author link templates. Applying the resource URI http://example.com/xy to the templates produces concrete links, and the order of links decides priority.
sections.eli5: A website can keep one standard note that tells programs where to find its rules and where to look for details about each page.

sections.title: Fetching the Document
sections.content:
A client gets the document by sending an HTTP (RFC 2616) or HTTPS (RFC 2818) GET request for /.well-known/host-meta on the default ports, 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS. Documents obtained by other protocols or ports have undefined scope and meaning. A server MUST support at least one of the two protocols, and if it supports both they MUST produce the same document.

If the response is a 301, 302 or 307, the client SHOULD try the location given, so a host's document may come from another host. If the resource is missing (for example 404 or 410), the client SHOULD infer that no metadata is available this way. The document SHOULD be served as application/xrd+xml.
sections.eli5: A program asks for the sign at a fixed spot on the website. If the sign is not there, the program learns the site has none.

sections.title: The host-meta Document and Link Templates
sections.content:
The document uses the XRD 1.0 format. Its root MUST be an XRD element. It SHOULD NOT include a Subject element, since no URI identifies a host, and using Alias is undefined and NOT RECOMMENDED. The subject of Property and Link elements is the host, except that for a Link with a template attribute the subject is the individual resource the template is applied to.

A Link with href states a relation between the host and a fixed target. One with template builds its target by applying the resource URI to the template. The only variable defined is uri, the entire context resource URI. Values are encoded as UTF-8 and every character other than unreserved ones MUST be percent-encoded. Protocols MAY define more variables but MUST NOT change the meaning of uri, and a client that cannot process a template SHOULD ignore that link.

Servers MAY offer other representations, chosen by the HTTP Accept header. With no Accept header, or for application/xrd+xml, the server MUST answer with the XRD XML form.
sections.eli5: A link in the note can be a fixed address, or a fill-in-the-blank address where the program writes the page it cares about into the blank.

sections.title: Processing host-meta Documents
sections.content:
Clients usually look for a link with a specific relation type, so they only process documents in order until they find what they want. A protocol using host-meta must say whether it wants host-wide or resource-specific information, and the order if it uses both.

For host-wide information the client MUST ignore every Link with a template attribute and every link using the lrdd relation type. Everything else is host-wide.

For resource-specific information the client applies the resource URI to each link template. Links with a relation other than lrdd are added to the resource descriptor in order. For an lrdd link the client fetches the LRDD document (following 301, 302 and 307 redirects over HTTP or HTTPS), then adds its links and properties in order, except any lrdd link, so inclusion is limited to a single level.
sections.eli5: For one page, the program fills in the blanks, collects the links in order, and also reads any extra note the site points to, but only one note deep.

sections.title: The JSON Form (JRD)
sections.content:
Appendix A defines JRD, a JSON representation of XRD using RFC 4627. A client MAY request it with Accept: application/json, and the server MUST answer with that Content-Type, otherwise it does not support JRD. Alternatively the client MAY request /.well-known/host-meta.json, and a server without JRD MUST answer 404. Servers are RECOMMENDED to offer JRD in addition to XRD.

The mapping is simple: Subject becomes subject, Expires becomes expires, Alias elements become an aliases array, Property elements become a properties object, and Link elements become a links array whose attributes are string pairs, with Title elements as titles. If several properties share a type only the last is kept. JRD does not carry XRD's extensibility.
sections.eli5: The same sign can also be written in a format that is easy for web programs to read.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Host-meta is meant for applications that explicitly opt in, and each must review the security implications itself. The RFC alone gives no guarantee that a document is controlled by the right entity. If the resource is compromised, it may put the server and its data at risk.

Applications that need authenticity MUST require HTTPS and MUST NOT produce a host-meta document by other means. They MUST also require that any redirect leading to the document uses HTTPS. Because the document speaks for the entire host, not just one scheme, host and port authority, applications MUST ensure that using it for another URI authority is not an exploit. Template authors must check that attackers cannot abuse templates, since unexpected characters in variable values could produce a malicious link.
sections.eli5: If a bad person could change the sign, they could send programs to the wrong places. So programs that need to trust it must fetch it over the secure kind of connection.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC registers two well-known URI suffixes, host-meta and host-meta.json, with the IETF as change controller. For each, documents fetched over HTTP and HTTPS on default ports MUST be identical.

It also registers the lrdd link relation type under RFC 5988. The relation refers to further information about the link's context, expressed as an LRDD resource. LRDD resources MUST have an application/xrd+xml representation and MAY have others.
sections.eli5: The official lists now include the sign's file names and the word that means 'more details are over here'.
